# Shared inbox ownership and escalation policy
Revision 1. Prepared by Codex for review; no organizational acceptance is recorded.

## Responsibility contract
Each incoming item has one accountable triage owner until a named receiver acknowledges it. Assignment to a squad makes the squad responsible for coordination, not every member responsible for the response. The triage owner checks workspace, source, existing related work and urgency before creating or linking a ticket.

## Routing table
| Input | Initial action | Receiver | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary question | Check existing answer and clarify missing context | Relevant domain agent or member | Receiver acknowledges the question and response scope |
| Reproducible defect | Capture expected/actual behavior and reproduction | Delivery squad | Linked ticket with reproducible input and owner |
| Suspected incident | Preserve impact and timestamps; stop speculative changes | Incident Commander | Incident scope and named responding owner |
| Unclear request | Ask for the missing decision; retain ownership | Original requester | Clarified outcome, not automatic escalation |
| Duplicate | Link the existing item without losing requester context | Current ticket owner | Existing owner confirms coverage |

## Escalation rules
Escalate immediately when current evidence indicates access leakage, loss of user records or interruption of a critical workflow. For ordinary questions, the workspace owner must set a response target before overdue escalation can be automated; this document supplies no invented service-level commitment. If a receiver declines or does not acknowledge, the triage owner remains accountable and asks the workspace owner to assign a receiver.

## Response acceptance
A response must cite the relevant deliverable/version or explicitly state that the requested work remains unperformed. A closed inbox message does not automatically close its ticket. Acceptance records identify the accepting member, scope accepted and unresolved work. Do not infer acceptance from a read receipt, emoji reaction or completed Run.

## Verification and open decisions
Exercise an ordinary question, duplicate, urgent report, declined handoff and a resolved response with an open follow-up. Confirm each retains one accountable owner and links its ticket. Actual roster acceptance, response targets and production inbox integration remain unverified.

## Criteria
The explicit acceptance/verification cases in this document require actual evidence before acceptance.

## Exclusions
No production execution, external storage certification, implicit owner approval or unsupported resume guarantee.

# Keyboard-accessible ticket relationship picker
Revision 1. Prepared by Codex; review requested. Implementation is not implied.

## Entry and search
An explicitly labelled Add relationship button opens the picker and moves focus to its search input. The dialog names the source ticket and relationship type. Search results are scoped by the server to the active workspace and current member's access. Never show a private title first and rely on navigation failure to enforce authorization.

## Keyboard contract
Tab reaches search, relationship-type selection, results and Cancel without entering the background page. Arrow keys move among selectable results when using a listbox pattern; Enter selects the active result once. Escape closes without applying a pending selection and returns focus to Add relationship. A result's accessible name includes identifier and title. Loading and no-results states are announced once, without changing the selected relationship type or discarding search text.

## Creation and removal
Prevent self-reference and duplicate pairs. Disable submission while it is in flight; present the server error without closing the picker. On success expose a navigable ticket identifier and relationship type in the source ticket. Removal is a separately labelled button available by keyboard, never only on hover. After removal place focus on the next relation or Add relationship when the list becomes empty.

## Boundaries and layout
Validate target access again when saving. If permission changes while the picker is open, reject the mutation without returning target content. At 390px, search and relation type fit the dialog width, long titles wrap, and Cancel remains reachable. The target link retains a return route to the source ticket in the same workspace.

## Acceptance evidence
Capture keyboard-only add, Escape without mutation, empty search, failed save/retry, duplicate rejection, removal of the last relation, long titles and access revoked between search and save. Record actual focus targets and persisted relation IDs. No execution result or design acceptance is recorded in this version.

# Resumable attachment upload implementation contract
Revision 1. Prepared by Codex for scope and engineering review. This is a requirements contract, not an implemented diff.

## Completion boundary
True resume means preserving a server-recognized transfer identity and continuing from an acknowledged offset. Restarting an upload request is a different capability. Before implementation, establish which behavior the backend actually supports and expose the corresponding action honestly.

## Required server contract
Initiation returns a workspace-bound transfer identity, expiry and continuation capability. Status returns authoritative acknowledged progress. Each write validates access, expected offset and transfer generation. Repeated identical writes must not append duplicated bytes. Finalization verifies integrity and atomically associates exactly one durable attachment with the ticket. These are proposed semantics, not existing endpoints claimed by this document.

## Client and cancellation
Retain local file access only while available. Treat progress as confirmed only after a server response. Serialize retries and ignore stale responses after cancellation or replacement. Authorization failure requires user action. On refresh, recover only if both transfer status and readable local bytes are available; otherwise ask for reselection or restart.

## Failure cases and required proof
| Case | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| Disconnect after partial acknowledgement | Same identity, correct offset, unchanged accepted bytes |
| Duplicate retry | No duplicate bytes or attachment record |
| Expired transfer | Explicit restart/reselect path; no false Resume promise |
| Cancel during reconnect | No queued request proceeds after cancellation |
| Workspace switch or access revoked | No cross-workspace association or content leak |
| Finalization response lost | Reconciliation finds one existing durable result |

## Dependencies and open work
SMART-13 defines accepted scope once actually reviewed; SMART-8 defines interaction; SMART-10 defines regression expectations. Existing local cleanup tests do not prove this protocol. A matching implementation diff, independent review, corrected findings, executed regression report and explicit release decision remain missing. The ticket was not started by writing this contract and no agent execution is asserted.

## Criteria
The explicit acceptance/verification cases in this document require actual evidence before acceptance.

## Exclusions
No production execution, external storage certification, implicit owner approval or unsupported resume guarantee.

    active = set()

from contextlib import contextmanager
import io
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import select

from workpal_backend.infrastructure.database import Database, migrate
from workpal_backend.infrastructure.jobs import jobs
from workpal_backend.files.models import upload_intent
from workpal_backend.files.repository import finalize_ready, reserve_intent
from workpal_backend.files.storage import LocalBlobStore


def wait_for(predicate, processes, timeout=10):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        for process in processes:
            assert process.poll() is None, 'CLI process exited before acceptance'
        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, 'Timed out waiting for durable recovery'
        time.sleep(.025)


@contextmanager
def cli(command, env, log):
    with log.open('wb') as output:
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, '-m', 'workpal_backend.cli', command],
            env=env, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        )
        try:
            yield process
        finally:
            was_running = process.poll() is None
            if was_running:
                process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                code = process.wait(timeout=5)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                process.kill()
                process.wait(timeout=5)
                raise AssertionError(f'{command} required SIGKILL: {log.read_text()}')
            assert was_running and code in ({0} if command == 'worker' else {0, -signal.SIGTERM}), f'{command} did not shut down gracefully ({code}): {log.read_text()}'


def test_cli_scheduled_recovery(settings, tmp_path):
    migrate(settings)
    root = tmp_path / 'bytes'
    root.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    store = LocalBlobStore(root)
    with socket.socket() as listener:
        listener.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
        port = listener.getsockname()[1]
    env = dict(os.environ, WORKPAL_DATABASE_URL=settings.database_url,
        WORKPAL_UPLOAD_DIR=str(root), WORKPAL_HOST='127.0.0.1', WORKPAL_PORT=str(port),
        WORKPAL_ENV='development', WORKPAL_DEV_AUTH='false',
        REDIS_URL=settings.redis_url, REDIS_KEY_PREFIX=f'test:recovery:{uuid4().hex}:',
        WORKPAL_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL='.05', WORKPAL_RECONCILE_INTERVAL='.05',
        PYTHONPATH=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'src'))
    db = Database(settings)
    payload = b'durable upload bytes\x00\xff'

    def rows():
        with db.transaction() as session:
            return {r['id']: dict(r) for r in session.execute(select(upload_intent)).mappings()}

    def api_up(process):
        def health():
            try:
                response = httpx.get(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health', timeout=.3)
                return response.status_code == 200 and response.json()['pid'] == process.pid
            except httpx.TransportError:
                return False
        wait_for(health, [process])

    try:
        # First lifecycle establishes actual API and scheduler processes before a restart.

# Upload recovery interaction specification
Revision: 1. Prepared by Codex during the current evidence repair. Review requested; no previous design approval is asserted.

## Scope and dependency
Defines the interaction consumed by SMART-7. It does not claim that byte-offset resume exists. A server must establish whether a transfer can continue before the UI offers Resume; otherwise offer Retry upload, which restarts the transfer without promising preserved progress.

## State model
| State | Entry condition | Visible content | Permitted actions | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uploading | Request accepted and progress available | Filename, determinate progress only when known, Cancel | Cancel | Complete, interrupted, authorization required, file unavailable |
| Interrupted | Retryable connection failure | Upload interrupted. Check your connection and try again. | Resume only with valid server capability; otherwise Retry upload; Cancel | Uploading after one explicit request or Cancelled |
| Authorization required | Server rejects authorization | Sign in to continue this upload. | Sign in; Cancel | Revalidate access and transfer identity before retry |
| File unavailable | Local bytes cannot be read | Select the file again to continue. | Choose file; Cancel | Validate new selection before any request |
| Cancelled | User cancels before completion | Upload cancelled | Remove; start a new upload | New transfer requires explicit action |
| Complete | Server confirms persisted attachment | Filename and open/download action | Open; remove association if authorized | No retry action |

## Transition rules
A network reconnect alone does not authorize repeated requests. Disable retry while a retry request is pending. Cancel invalidates the active request generation so late success or progress from it cannot restore an Uploading state. Authentication failure never enters an automatic retry loop. If the server cannot prove transfer identity, do not merge partial data or present the old progress as current.

## Reselection
Validate filename, size and the server's required content identity before reusing an upload. A matching filename alone is insufficient. If identity cannot be established, explain that a fresh upload is required. Do not overwrite an already accepted attachment silently.

## Keyboard and announcements
Tab order follows filename/context, recovery action, Cancel. Use native buttons; Enter and Space activate once. On failure keep focus in the upload area; do not steal focus from another field. After retry preserve focus on the same action or its stable container while disabled. Announce state changes politely once; throttle progress updates rather than announcing every chunk. Authorization and file selection dialogs return focus to their triggering control.

## Narrow layout
At 390px the filename may wrap and controls occupy a separate row. Progress and failure text must not obscure actions; actions remain reachable without hover or horizontal scrolling.

## Acceptance cases
Disconnect once and repeatedly; expire authorization before retry; cancel during reconnect; return from authentication without access; reselect different bytes with the same name; lose the file on refresh; receive late success after cancellation. For each case capture actual browser behavior and request count. Expected behavior is defined above; execution is not recorded by this specification.

## Handoff and open decisions
SMART-7 must identify the actual resume API and supported identity checks. SMART-10 owns the regression report. Until those exist the Resume option is conditional, and acceptance remains open. No release authority is delegated by this document.

"""Exercise durable upload recovery through real CLI process lifecycles."""
from contextlib import contextmanager
import io
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import select

from workpal_backend.infrastructure.database import Database, migrate
from workpal_backend.infrastructure.jobs import jobs
from workpal_backend.files.models import upload_intent
from workpal_backend.files.repository import finalize_ready, reserve_intent
from workpal_backend.files.storage import LocalBlobStore


def wait_for(predicate, processes, timeout=10):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        for process in processes:
            assert process.poll() is None, 'CLI process exited before acceptance'
        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, 'Timed out waiting for durable recovery'
        time.sleep(.025)


@contextmanager
def cli(command, env, log):
    with log.open('wb') as output:
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, '-m', 'workpal_backend.cli', command],
            env=env, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        )
        try:
            yield process
        finally:
            was_running = process.poll() is None
            if was_running:
                process.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                code = process.wait(timeout=5)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                process.kill()
                process.wait(timeout=5)
                raise AssertionError(f'{command} required SIGKILL: {log.read_text()}')
            assert was_running and code in ({0} if command == 'worker' else {0, -signal.SIGTERM}), f'{command} did not shut down gracefully ({code}): {log.read_text()}'


def test_cli_scheduled_recovery(settings, tmp_path):
    migrate(settings)
    root = tmp_path / 'bytes'
    root.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    store = LocalBlobStore(root)
    with socket.socket() as listener:
        listener.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
        port = listener.getsockname()[1]
    env = dict(os.environ, WORKPAL_DATABASE_URL=settings.database_url,
        WORKPAL_UPLOAD_DIR=str(root), WORKPAL_HOST='127.0.0.1', WORKPAL_PORT=str(port),
        WORKPAL_ENV='development', WORKPAL_DEV_AUTH='false',
        REDIS_URL=settings.redis_url, REDIS_KEY_PREFIX=f'test:recovery:{uuid4().hex}:',
        WORKPAL_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL='.05', WORKPAL_RECONCILE_INTERVAL='.05',
        PYTHONPATH=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'src'))
    db = Database(settings)
    payload = b'durable upload bytes\x00\xff'

    def rows():
        with db.transaction() as session:
            return {r['id']: dict(r) for r in session.execute(select(upload_intent)).mappings()}

    def api_up(process):
        def health():
            try:
                response = httpx.get(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health', timeout=.3)
                return response.status_code == 200 and response.json()['pid'] == process.pid
            except httpx.TransportError:
                return False
        wait_for(health, [process])

    try:
        # First lifecycle establishes actual API and scheduler processes before a restart.
        with cli('serve', env, tmp_path / 'api-before.log') as api:
            api_up(api)
            with cli('worker', env, tmp_path / 'worker-before.log') as worker:
                def scheduler_completed_cycle():
                    with db.transaction() as session:
                        job = session.execute(select(jobs).where(jobs.c.name == 'files.reconcile')).mappings().first()
                        return job is not None and job['token'] is None and job['last_error'] is None
                wait_for(scheduler_completed_cycle, [api, worker])
            with db.transaction() as session:
                expired = reserve_intent(session, {'owner_id': 'owner'}, {}, store.new_key(), now=1)
                published = reserve_intent(session, {'owner_id': 'owner'}, {}, store.new_key(), now=1)
                live = reserve_intent(session, {'owner_id': 'owner'}, {}, store.new_key(), lease_seconds=3600)
                ready = reserve_intent(session, {'owner_id': 'owner'}, {}, store.new_key())
            for row in (expired, published, live, ready):
                with store.create_staging(row['storage_key'], row['staging_key']) as stream:
                    size, digest = store.write_bounded(stream, io.BytesIO(payload), 1024)
                if row in (published, ready):
                    store.sync_and_promote(row['storage_key'], row['staging_key'])
            with db.transaction() as session:
                finalize_ready(session, ready['id'], ready['lease_token'],
                    {'size_bytes': size, 'sha256': digest, 'filename': 'ready.bin'})
            before = rows()
            assert before[expired['id']]['state'] == before[published['id']]['state'] == 'pending'
            assert before[ready['id']]['state'] == 'ready'
        with cli('serve', env, tmp_path / 'api-after.log') as api:
            api_up(api)
            # API startup must not do scheduler work.
            assert rows() == before
            with cli('worker', env, tmp_path / 'worker-after.log') as worker:
                wait_for(lambda: expired['id'] not in rows() and published['id'] not in rows(), [api, worker])
                time.sleep(.2)  # Observe additional scheduling cycles protecting survivors.
                assert rows() == {live['id']: before[live['id']], ready['id']: before[ready['id']]}
                assert not (root / store._name(expired['storage_key'], expired['staging_key'])).exists()
                assert not (root / store._name(published['storage_key'])).exists()
                assert (root / store._name(live['storage_key'], live['staging_key'])).read_bytes() == payload
                with store.open_ready(ready['storage_key']) as stream:
                    assert stream.read() == payload
                assert set(p.name for p in root.iterdir()) == {
                    store._name(live['storage_key'], live['staging_key']), store._name(ready['storage_key'])}
    finally:
        db.close()

# Attachment recovery requirements
Revision: 1. Prepared by Codex in the current evidence repair. Proposed requirements; historical acceptance is not confirmed.

## User outcome
A user knows whether an interrupted upload can continue, must restart, requires sign-in, or needs the local file selected again. No action creates duplicate accepted attachments or hides a failure behind a success message.

## Functional requirements
R1. Keep the filename and last confirmed server progress visible while the local file remains readable. Do not label estimated or restarted progress as acknowledged progress.
R2. Distinguish retryable connection failure, denied/expired authorization, unavailable file and explicit cancellation.
R3. Reuse transfer identity only when the backend validates that identity and continuation capability. Otherwise restart explicitly; do not claim byte-offset resume.
R4. An explicit retry starts at most one active request. Pending retries cannot be duplicated by repeated clicks.
R5. Cancelling prevents queued retries and ignores late completion for that request generation.
R6. Completion requires the server's durable attachment acknowledgement, not a client progress value of 100 percent.
R7. Every request rechecks workspace membership and attachment association. Switching workspaces must not transfer an attachment to another ticket implicitly.

## Acceptance matrix
| Requirement | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| R1/R3 | Server API contract, transfer identity and byte progress captured before/after interruption |
| R2 | Browser recordings/screenshots of each distinct error and available action |
| R4/R5 | Request trace proving single retry and no retry after cancellation |
| R6 | Persistence test and reload showing accepted attachment |
| R7 | Two-workspace and revoked-membership tests with no leaked metadata or content |

## Exclusions
No recovery promise after local bytes are lost; no automatic production release; no external-storage certification without an accessible test environment; no migration of attachments between workspaces; no inference that cleanup of expired upload intents proves partial-transfer resume.

## Inputs and downstream ownership
SMART-8 specifies interactions. SMART-7 must deliver implementation and review. SMART-10 supplies the measured regression report. SMART-17 requires a separate release decision. The current local upload verification confirms selected cleanup/HTTP behaviors only; its uncovered scope remains mandatory before full delivery acceptance.

## Open decisions
The backend continuation API and file identity algorithm have not been established in this audit. Product owner must decide whether explicit restart is sufficient for this scope or true byte-offset resume is required. This document does not record that decision on their behalf.

## Criteria
R1–R7 and the acceptance matrix in this document require actual evidence before acceptance.

## Exclusions
No production execution, external storage certification, implicit owner approval or unsupported resume guarantee.

# Empty inbox interaction and copy specification
Revision: 1. Prepared by Codex during evidence repair. Review requested; does not assert historical owner acceptance or implemented behavior.

## State selection
Only show an empty state after a successful response. Loading, request failure and permission denial are separate states and must not be rendered as an empty inbox.

| Condition | Heading | Supporting text | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Successful unfiltered result with zero messages | You're all caught up | New work will appear here. | None required |
| Successful filtered result with zero matches | No matching messages | Try changing your filters. | Clear filters |
| Loading | Loading messages… | Preserve existing results if revalidating | No empty-state action |
| Failed request | Unable to load messages | Try again. | Retry |

## Filter reset contract
Clear filters resets only the active inbox filters, not workspace, selected ticket or other saved views. Re-fetch or rederive the result using the same workspace. Announce the resulting count once after completion. Keep focus on a stable filter control after the clear action disappears; do not send focus to the document body. # External storage recovery verification protocol
Revision 1. Prepared by Codex. Execution blocked: no external storage environment was used by this audit.

## Environment prerequisites
An authorized isolated storage account/bucket, disposable test objects, documented retention/cleanup rules and a credential delivery channel are required. Do not paste secrets into Activity or reports. Record backend revision, storage adapter version, region/endpoint class and sanitized configuration before execution.

## Test procedure
1. Upload a known small payload and record its digest and durable attachment identifier.
2. Interrupt a larger upload during transfer; record the acknowledgement boundary and resulting server state.
3. Retry using only capabilities that the adapter supports; compare final bytes and count durable objects and associations.
4. Expire authorization, then retry; verify an explicit error with no unauthorized object/metadata access.
5. Cancel while reconnect is pending; verify cancellation wins over late callbacks.
6. Simulate storage success followed by metadata-write failure; verify the documented reconciliation path and absence of accidental deletion of a committed object.
7. Revoke workspace access and attempt read, download and retry.
8. Remove only the disposable objects belonging to this test and record cleanup outcome.

For each step capture start/end time, command or browser action, exact source revision, sanitized response/request trace, expected outcome, actual outcome and pass/fail/not-run. Attach original logs and digest comparison. A skipped step is uncovered scope, never a pass.
